images.title: Jumping back on the line
images.purpose: Show that taking away 4/7 from 6/7 means jumping back 4 equal gaps of 1/7 on the number line, landing on 2/7.
images.composition: One long horizontal number line across the middle with generous space above for the jump arcs, and one equation centred below the line.
images.exact_structure: A horizontal number line from 0 to 1 cut into exactly 7 equal gaps by 8 evenly spaced tick marks. A teal #0072B2 dot sits on the tick at 6/7. Four equal amber #E69F00 arcs above the line each span exactly one gap, going left from 6/7 to 5/7, 4/7, 3/7 and 2/7, with a small arrowhead on each pointing left. A reddish purple #CC79A7 dot marks the landing tick at 2/7. Only the ticks 0, 2/7, 6/7 and 1 carry labels. Exactly 1 line, 8 ticks, 4 arcs, 2 dots.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
tick marks that are not evenly spaced, or arcs that span more or less than one gap
images.takeaway: To take away, jump back across equal gaps.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 1 in 7 equal gaps; from a dot at 6/7, four arcs jump back one gap each and land on 2/7, showing 6/7 − 4/7 = 2/7.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the gaps crossed, not the marks, while tracing the arcs from 6/7.

image_decisions.why: Jumping back equal gaps on a number line is a picture idea; one clean line with four arcs carries it.
